We’re looking for a Member of Technical Staff intern to work hand-in-hand with our founders and team

This is a hands-on role that combines engineering, storytelling, and community. You'll ship code alongside our product and engineering teams, and work closely with our GTM and DevRel teams to turn what we build into demos, content, and experiences that inspire builders.

You'll be part of our mission of connecting AI agents to the web.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Take part in the development of new products and features built on top of Linkup's proprietary index.

- Develop and maintain SDKs, templates, integrations, and reference implementations for AI and agentic workflows.

- Build and ship polished demos, sample apps, and starter kits that showcase what's possible with Linkup's APIs.

- Produce technical content: blog posts, tutorials, videos, and benchmarks that make complex tech approachable.

- Collect and synthesize developer feedback to inform product and developer experience priorities.

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Every demo, integration, and product you build helps define how AI agents connect to the web.

You'll operate on the frontier between product and developers, bringing the voice of builders into everything we build and say.

If you love blending engineering with impact, building things developers actually use: this role is for you.

YOU'RE A GREAT FIT IF YOU

- Have high agency: you see something that should exist, and you build it. You don't wait to be told what to do.

What would be a big plus:

- Hands-on experience with APIs, LLMs, agents, and DevTools.

- A taste for turning technical depth into compelling storytelling.

- Participation in active developer communities, hackathons, or open-source projects.
.

DETAILS

You'll work shoulder to shoulder with the founders and the team, with real ownership from day one: your work ships to production and reaches thousands of developers.

ABOUT LINKUP

OUR VISION

We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web. These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information.

AI agents need web search. To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off.

Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs. Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space.

Web 2.0 is sunsetting. The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google's ad‑driven model has no natural home.

Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up. We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone.

Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup.

OUR MISSION

Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve.

Our mission is to deliver the world's freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs.

OUR CULTURE

Our culture is built on the following values:

- Mission. We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents.

- Speed. We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well.

- Ownership. We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion.

- Teamwork. Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset.

- Humility. We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences.

We expect all team members to take an active role in shaping our company culture.

OUR TEAM

We are a small technical team, working shoulder to shoulder to build the web of agents.

About the Role

OpenGov is looking for Product Engineer Interns who are eager to learn what it means to own a product — from customer discovery through delivery. This internship is built around a new kind of role born from AI's ability to handle execution work that once required multiple specialists. What AI cannot do is decide what matters, talk to customers, make the right call in ambiguous situations, or own whether a product succeeds. That is what Product Engineers learn to do — and this internship is where that journey starts.

This role is first and foremost about developing product thinking — not becoming a developer. The best interns will be the ones who grow genuinely curious about customers: who they are, what they actually need, and what outcomes depend on solving their problems. The engineering side — using AI-native tooling to write code, build interfaces — is a skill you will be introduced to and encouraged to develop. It is a career accelerator, not a day-one requirement.

If you have a background or strong interest in product management, UX design, engineering, or some combination — and you want real ownership of a problem rather than a slide deck — this internship is for you.

"Product Engineer" is two words — but the first word is the one that matters most. The second is how you get there.

The 10-week internship will run from June 7, 2027 through August 13, 2027.

What You'll Work On

- A scoped product problem: a defined set of customers, problems, and outcomes — sized for a 10–12 week engagement with real impact.

- Customer discovery: you will conduct or observe customer conversations and translate what you learn into product decisions.

- User experience flows: you will define interaction patterns within an existing design system and validate them with users.

- AI-assisted delivery: using AI-native tooling, you will move from intent to spec to working prototype — supported by your team, but accountable for the output.

- Metrics: you will define what success looks like for your area and track it throughout the internship.

How AI Works in This Role

AI-native tooling handles a significant portion of what product managers and designers have historically spent their time on. As an intern, you will be hands-on with these tools from day one:

- Spec writing: AI drafts the first spec from your intent statement. You learn to review, sharpen, and own what gets built.

- UX design: AI generates mockups from the design system based on your flow definitions. You make the product decisions within it.

- Research synthesis: AI clusters and themes interview notes and support data. You interpret what it means and make the call.

- Release content: AI generates release notes and enablement materials from shipped features. You review and refine them.

- Test coverage: AI generates test cases from acceptance criteria. You learn to write criteria precise enough to verify.

What AI does not do: understand your customers, make the call on what matters, own the outcome, or build the cross-functional trust that makes things ship. That is the job — and what you will be learning.

- Participate in customer discovery conversations; synthesize what you hear into defensible product decisions.

- Define user experience flows and interaction patterns within the existing design system.

- Write intent documents that AI tooling can execute against; review AI-generated specs for accuracy and completeness.

- Partner with your engineering and product mentor to resolve ambiguity in real time during the development cycle.

- Track adoption and usage metrics for your scoped area; use them to drive iteration.

- Present your product area and findings in a final intern showcase — covering the customer problem, what you built, and what you would do next.

- Surface gaps, risks, and unanswered questions proactively; don't wait to be asked.

- Currently pursuing a degree in computer science, information systems, product design, HCI, business, or a closely adjacent field — or equivalent self-directed experience.

- Comfort with ambiguity and speed: you make reasonable decisions with incomplete information rather than waiting for certainty.

- Willingness to grow into code fluency using AI-native tooling — you don't need to arrive as a developer, but you must be willing to get there.

- Prior exposure to product management, UX design, software development, or customer research is a plus — in any form (coursework, projects, prior internships, side work).

- Familiarity with design tools (Figma, etc.) or development tooling is welcome but not required.
